title: Ivo and the Glasshouse
premise: Casper Fairweather, a bridge inspector who measures everything and owns nothing, discovers a box of undelivered letters hidden behind her late aunt's wardrobe in the family glasshouse estate. The letters reveal that the family patriarch's death twenty years ago was not an accident, and that every member of the household — including Casper's own mother — arranged their lives around the silence. As Casper traces the letters' intended recipient, she must decide whether exposing the truth will save or shatter the only family she has left. In the end, she delivers the final letter publicly at the estate's auction, choosing truth over belonging, and walks away owning nothing but the story itself.
about_author: Sable Pemberton is the pen name of a former structural engineer who spent a decade inspecting bridges across the American Midwest before turning to fiction. Her work examines the quiet architecture of families — the load-bearing lies and hairline fractures that hold households together until they don't.

chapters.title: Expansion Joints
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper inspects the Harrow Bridge by day and drifts through her marriage to Theo by night, measuring distances in millimeters because it is easier than naming them. A summons arrives: her estranged aunt Vivian has died, leaving Casper the glasshouse on the Fairweather estate. Emotional beat: numb routine cracked open by obligation.

chapters.title: The Tenant's Key
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper returns to Glasshouse, the crumbling family estate, where her mother Ruth, uncle Desmond, and cousin Imogen have already gathered like heirs circling. She is given a key but not a welcome; the family speaks in a coded warmth she can't parse. Emotional beat: the ache of being kin without being kept.

chapters.title: Behind the Wardrobe
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Alone in the glasshouse annex, Casper finds a cavity behind Vivian's wardrobe containing forty-one undelivered letters, all addressed to a 'M. Okafor,' spanning two decades. The earliest letter trembles with fear; the last is dated three days after grandfather Edmund's fatal fall. Emotional beat: discovery as vertigo.

chapters.title: What the Family Arranged
chapters.summary: POV: Casper, with an interlude letter from Vivian (1987). Reading the letters, Casper learns Edmund's death coincided with his plan to sell the estate and disinherit everyone; the letters suggest Vivian witnessed something. At dinner, the family performs grief for a woman they barely visited. Emotional beat: suspicion blooming under civility.

chapters.title: M. Okafor
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper tracks down Miriam Okafor, now elderly, once the estate's gardener — and learns Miriam never received a single letter because someone intercepted them. Miriam recognizes Casper's face before her name and says only: 'You have her hands.' Emotional beat: the past reaching out through resemblance.

chapters.title: The Weight Test
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Miriam reveals that Edmund fell from the glasshouse roof the night he caught young Theo's father — Casper's father, Daniel — sabotaging the roof beams to force the sale. Daniel fled; Vivian stayed silent to protect him, mailing nothing ever again. Casper realizes her inheritance is complicity. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth beginning their war.

chapters.title: Hairline Fractures
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper confronts Ruth, who admits she always knew why Daniel left and chose the family's silence over her daughter's questions. Desmond, sensing exposure, moves to fast-track the estate sale and have the glasshouse demolished. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing the mask of protection.

chapters.title: Load-Bearing Lies
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The family offers Casper a settlement to sign away the glasshouse and its secrets; Imogen, desperate for her share, begs her to take it. Theo arrives uninvited, offering Casper the one honest conversation of their marriage — too late to be a home, just in time to be a mirror. Emotional beat: the price of belonging made explicit.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Climax. At the estate auction, with bidders assembled and demolition crews waiting, Casper takes the podium instead of the buyer's table and reads Vivian's final letter aloud — the confession Vivian wrote and never sent. The room fractures; Desmond storms out; Ruth does not look away. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, delivered in a dead woman's voice.

chapters.title: Owner of Nothing
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Resolution. The sale collapses into litigation no one wins; the glasshouse stands, unowned, its panes catching light. Casper delivers the last letter to Miriam by hand, then drives back across the Harrow Bridge — inspecting it one final time, knowing exactly what holds and what gives. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into freedom.
